title: The training lake: one store, one record shape per task, every row's origin, consent and split (with 26.2, 27.1, 27.3)
request: Phases 4 and 5: DCLab's own decision models and an ML-solver model, with every piece of data they need collected under the hood, organised, structured and clean. The owner's answers: OpenML yes; Claude's outputs evaluation only; the owner trains on a GPU.
spec: dclab_core.lake (DecisionSample, TrainingExample, GoldManifest, Provenance, origins, gold_problems); dclab_rnd/lake (bronze, silver, gold; make lake); OpenML real tables; verified self-play; the committed manifest.
plan: Write the record shapes and the rules first.
Read every source through its existing consent gate.
Fetch real tables once and keep only bands.
Solve invented problems and keep only verified solves.

decisions.decision: The lake reads a workspace only through the sets make datasets wrote under its train consent.
decisions.why: Those sets already apply the workspace, project and draft consent, storage and grouping; a second reader would bypass them (review).

decisions.decision: DCLab's build history is evaluation only until the owner decides.
decisions.why: It was written in Claude Code sessions, so it is a Claude output under the owner's decision about Claude's outputs.

decisions.decision: A training row identical to an evaluation row is dropped, whatever its group.
decisions.why: Banded features repeat across tables; an identical input in train and sealed measures recall, not judgement.

change: dclab_core/lake.py (new), contracts, conformance, CHANGELOG 0.59.0, schemas; dclab_rnd/lake/__init__.py, __main__.py, openml.py, selfplay.py (new); Makefile lake; .gitignore lake/; tests/test_training_lake.py (new); plan, integration guide, CLAUDE.md, catalog. Also dclab_rnd/lake/train.py (export) and TRAINING.md; studio/data.py (the positive class); draft/api.py (the one-step build).

findings.defect: The new tests overwrote an existing test file and deleted 21 passing tests.
findings.scenario: tests/test_lake.py held the 23.10 suite; the lake tests were written over it.
findings.cause: The file name was taken without checking.
findings.fix: The suite is restored; the lake tests are in tests/test_training_lake.py.

findings.defect: Drafts were read as files, so on PostgreSQL every Claude session was dropped.
findings.scenario: The owner's dev workspace keeps drafts in the database.
findings.cause: The builder read the workspace folder directly.
findings.fix: The lake reads only what make datasets wrote, through storage.

findings.defect: Twin folders were read with no consent check and labelled as the owner's.
findings.scenario: A collected tester's workspace with consent off still entered the lake.
findings.cause: The twin folder was read directly.
findings.fix: Claude's answers arrive only through the twin sets, built under the workspace's and each project's consent.

findings.defect: A withdrawn consent was not honoured until the next sweep.
findings.scenario: Train switched off at 10:00, make lake at 10:05: the withdrawn rows went into gold.
findings.cause: The set manifests' use field was trusted.
findings.fix: The workspace's current switch and the stale marker are checked; an improve-only set is counted and not read.

findings.defect: Stale gold sets were never removed.
findings.scenario: A refused set or a withdrawn point kept its old rows for training to read.
findings.fix: Silver and gold are rebuilt whole each time.

findings.scenario: About 45% of train rows were identical to dev or sealed rows.
findings.cause: The dedupe key held the group, which is in one split.
findings.fix: The key is the point, features and label; a train row identical to dev or sealed, and a dev row identical to sealed, are dropped and counted.

findings.defect: A teacher row's input was not what Claude saw.
findings.scenario: 12 of 58 replies included a message posted after Claude's request.
findings.cause: The input was rebuilt from the draft by time.
findings.fix: Teacher rows come from the twin sets, which keep the step's own input.

findings.defect: The expert design target was not redacted.
findings.scenario: Claude's restatement of the person's words went in raw.
findings.fix: Designs come from the twin sets, redacted by their builder.

findings.defect: Each set's dropped counts were wrong.
findings.scenario: Every decision set showed every source's drops.
findings.fix: Drops are counted per source and merged into the sets each source feeds; the summary lists them by source.

findings.defect: Workflow decisions were labelled as column decisions.
findings.scenario: A draft's next-question decision became a column sample.
findings.cause: Every subject kind but column was turned into column.
findings.fix: The ledger's kinds map to column, dataset, problem or step.

findings.defect: Teacher rows were grouped under another name than the decisions of the same session.
findings.scenario: A model trained on a project's decisions could be compared with Claude on the same session.
findings.cause: The group was the draft id, not the project.
findings.fix: The twin sets' groups come from group_of, the same in every set.

findings.defect: The failure paths were not tested.
findings.scenario: Removing the consent or sealed branches left the suite green.
findings.cause: Only the happy path was tested.
findings.fix: Tests for consent off, improve only, stale, withdrawal, a sealed row outside sealed, decontamination, OpenML labels and masking.

findings.defect: The outcome was always the last option of the target question.
findings.scenario: A model could learn its position, not the table.
findings.cause: It was appended to keep it among the first 60.

findings.defect: A self-play leakage answer was not learnable from its input.
findings.scenario: The engine found the leak from a train-only signal the input did not show.
findings.cause: The input held only the column bands.
findings.fix: The auditor's train-only signals are part of the input.

findings.defect: A one-step build made the genuine class the positive one.
findings.scenario: Live replay: fake_return against genuine_or_no_return; the agent had to turn it round.
findings.cause: No exact event word matched, so the alphabetical last class won.
findings.fix: Event words inside a class name pick it; with none, the rarer class; an explicit yes or 1 first as before.

findings.defect: A one-step build made an anomaly project with no outcome on a labelled table.
findings.scenario: Live replay: the words read nothing labelled while the simulated table named is_fake_return; the agent had to set the target.
findings.cause: The card's anomaly family skipped the supervised solution.
findings.fix: A named outcome column means a supervised solution whatever the card inferred.

measurements.name: the first lake build
measurements.result: every set written; generated decisions decontaminated; OpenML tables arriving; Claude answers only in eval_only
limits: The workspaces' own sets are empty until their train consent and each project's consent are on.

outcome: One lake every DCLab model reads, organised by task, with every row's origin and consent, rebuilt whole and checked.
lessons: Read data through the gate that already applies consent; never beside it.
Check a file name exists before writing a new test file.
risks: Most workspace sets hold rows only once a project's consent is on; the lake's real-session content is near empty today.
